patch.value: selfhost.bundle crossed GitHub's 50 MB warning and grows with every commit toward the 100 MB push limit

On 2026-10-12, pushing the close-out branch warned that selfhost.bundle is 50.53 MB, above GitHub's recommended 50 MB maximum. The bundle is regenerated for every commit, including tracker-only commits, and grows with history; at 100 MB GitHub rejects the push outright, which would block every PR and release. Options: an incremental or thin bundle against a recorded base, compressing or pruning objects that are not needed for self-host verification, moving the full bundle to a release asset with only its digest committed, or Git LFS (which needs evaluation against the self-host contract).

A committed self-host artifact stays well below 50 MB as history grows (measured over a projected year of commits), accept:self-host still proves byte-identity of the committed source, and pushes no longer emit the GitHub large-file warning.

The committed self-host artifact stays well below GitHub's 50 MiB per-file warning as history grows (measured over a projected year of commits), accept:self-host still proves byte-identity of the committed source, and pushes no longer emit the large-file warning.

Each commit that changes the self-hosted source or tracker data regenerates the bundle, so it grows with history. GitHub rejects a single repository file over 100 MiB, so any pull request or release commit that adds or updates selfhost.bundle as a Git file would then be blocked. Release assets have a separate, much larger limit, and the release workflow checks the committed bundle without adding it to its release commit. value.text: pi-agent (re-applied from the duplicate branch record): Measured before/after, bytes and MiB. BEFORE (origin/main HEAD, 2026-10-11): 49,260,541 bytes = 46.88 MiB (49.26 MB decimal); a day earlier 46,172,923 bytes = 44.13 MiB. Growth over the last 30 days of main: 14,240,151 -> 49,260,541 bytes across 15 bundle regenerations = +35,020,390 bytes (33.40 MiB), ~1.11 MiB/day, ~2.22 MiB per regeneration. Linear projection of the old design to one year: ~475.3 MB (~452 MiB); crosses the 50 MiB per-file warning within ~3 days and GitHub's 100 MiB hard rejection in ~48 days (~2026-11-28). AFTER (this branch's HEAD commit): 7,433,859 bytes = 7.08 MiB (7.43 MB decimal), a 6.62x reduction. Growth per regeneration is now zero by construction (the bundle replaces its snapshot instead of accumulating); residual growth is source-driven: the equivalent snapshot bundle grew 4,037,205 -> 7,394,951 bytes over the same window (~0.106 MiB/day, ~39 MiB/yr linear, projected ~46 MiB in one year, still below the 50 MiB warning). Gates: npm run release:check pass (with HOME/GIT_CONFIG isolation for CI identity), bun run release:check pass, coverage 100/100/100/100, node --test test/self-host.test.ts 58/58 pass; accept:self-host passes at the branch HEAD against the committed 7.08 MiB bundle.
